newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Jan inflation said lowest in 15 years.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Jan inflation said lowest in 15 years.

text.p: Colombian Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo, in a sneak preview of inflation figures to be released Saturday, said price increases in January were the lowest for the month in 15 years.

Ocampo did not specify the actual increase in the consumer price index for January. But in remarks to reporters, he said he expected the number to print a full percentage point below January 1996, when the CPI rose 2.5 percent.
"There's going to be good news about inflation and interest rates," Ocampo said.
He did not elaborate, but in December, a time of increased credit demand, the annualized 90-day CD rate fell by 70 baiss points to 27.9 percent.

Inflation last year totaled a higher-than-expected 21.6 percent. Mauricio Cardenas, head of Colombia's prestigious economic think tank Fedesarrollo, revised his forecast for 1997 inflation from 19 to 20 percent Thursday, citing what he called additional price pressures from the government's recent decision to clamp a six percent tax on all new foreign loans.
